content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing sustained upward trends.
- After sharp spikes in true values (e.g., 36.62, 38.18), forecasts lag and undershoot the actual peak.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overestimates after low points and underestimates after high points.
- Forecasts often fail to capture late-period volatility or sudden upward moves (e.g., 36.84, 36.37).
- Model underestimates true values in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, especially when true values are rising.
- Overshoots are common after low-to-mid range values, suggesting model reacts too aggressively to recent dips.
- Model lacks sensitivity to true value volatility in the last 7–10 days, leading to persistent underestimation.
